meta.subject: Revamp transaction_log_tr into lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc
meta.author: LIS Team

slides.headline:
Corporate Special Blood Category
on Merge and Deletion
slides.lede: Move patient merge, change-HKID and deletion handling out of the database trigger and into lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc, behind a per-hospital flag.
slides.footer: Design status: draft  ·  for CP3 review
slides.notes: LIS-10583, a change request against lis-patient-pmi-sync-svc. We are retiring the transaction_log trigger that maintains corporate special blood requirements and rebuilding that behaviour in the PMI sync service, gated per hospital. Target date needs reconfirming — every date on the ticket has lapsed.

slides.title: What we will cover

items.title: Background
items.note: why the trigger is still there

slides.notes: Incremental review. The bulk of the time should go on the routing and the two handlers.

slides.title: How we got here

steps.title: Trigger maintains the requirements
steps.body: Copied and reset by a database trigger on transaction_log.

steps.title: Sync service takes over PMI
steps.body: It took over merge and change-HKID, but blood category stayed in the database.

steps.title: Move the last piece
steps.body: Two mechanisms now touch the same records. The trigger is what is left.

callout.text: database-tier logic is invisible to service logging and cannot be switched off per hospital.

slides.notes: The trigger is not broken — it is simply the last piece of patient handling still living in the database while everything around it moved to the service.

slides.title: Which events matter

rows: Copy active requirements old → new HKID
Copy active requirements old → new HKID

takeaways.title: Two already arrive
takeaways.body: A40 and A47 already reach the service for the PID merge — we extend an existing path.

takeaways.title: One is new
takeaways.body: A29 is not received today. It is the only new subscription in this change.

slides.notes: Worth dwelling on the last column. Two of the three events already reach the service, so most of this is extending an existing handler. A29 is the genuinely new piece.

slides.title: What the trigger does today

lines.text: FOR each latest active category per blood_key
AND no active record on new HKID

findings.title: Invisible to service logging
findings.body: Runs in the database tier, so nothing appears in ALS beside the merge it belongs to.

findings.title: No per-hospital switch
findings.body: On or off for the whole database. No way to pilot a single site.

findings.title: Deletion never reaches us
findings.body: A29 is handled entirely by the trigger — the service never sees a deletion.

slides.footnote: Behaviour is preserved exactly: same records, same reset values, same corp_alert_status.
slides.notes: The behaviour itself is correct and stays correct. What we are fixing is where it lives — three consequences of that, on the right.

slides.title: Proposed routing

start.text:
Merge, change-HKID
or deletion message
arrives

fallthrough.label: No
fallthrough.title: Skip
fallthrough.body: Merge still completes; skip recorded in ALS

condition.label: Feature gate
condition.note: Read from lab_option per hospital server, so sites can be switched on one at a time.

slides.notes: One gate, then a two-way split. The important property is that when the flag is off the patient merge still completes normally — the blood category work is skipped, not failed.

slides.title: The two handlers

left.label: A40 / A47
left.title: Merge or change HKID
points: Only when blood_value = 1 and the new HKID has none

callout.text: set corp_alert_status = 21 on every record written, matching the trigger.

slides.notes: The asymmetry worth calling out: a merge failure rolls back the whole merge, because leaving a patient merged without their requirements would be clinically wrong. Deletion has no such coupling.

slides.title: The per-hospital flag

rows: Per hospital server — each site switches independently

takeaways.title: Off is safe
takeaways.body: With the flag off the merge completes as it does today and the skip is recorded in ALS. Nothing fails.

takeaways.title: No new table
takeaways.body: This reuses the existing lab_option setup — no schema change and no new configuration mechanism.

slides.notes: This is also the fallback switch. Turning a site off needs no deployment, which is why it is the first line in the fallback plan.

slides.title: Scope of change

steps.title: Rebuild the trigger's behaviour
steps.body: Move the copy and reset logic into the service, preserving values exactly.

steps.title: Hook the existing merge path
steps.body: Call it after a successful merge for A40 and A47 — both already handled.

steps.title: Subscribe to A29
steps.body: Add the deletion subscription and route it to the reset handler.

steps.title: Audit and regress
steps.body: ALS on every decision and skip; regress all three events, flag on and off.

sidebar.headline: One owner
sidebar.body: Patient merge already lives in the service. Leaving blood category in a trigger means two mechanisms on the same records.

slides.notes: Four work items, one of which — the A29 subscription — is genuinely new. Everything else extends a path that already runs in production.

slides.title: How this goes out

cards.title: Deploy dark
cards.body: Release the service with the component and the A29 subscription, flag off everywhere.

cards.title: Enable one site
cards.body: Set the flag for a single hospital and watch ALS for merge, change-HKID and deletion.

cards.title: Verify both states
cards.body: Confirm all three events behave correctly with the flag both on and off.

cards.title: Retire the trigger
cards.body: Only after a parallel run shows both paths writing the same records.

callout.text: the trigger stays live while the flag is on. Both paths skip when the new HKID already has an active record, so neither double-writes.

slides.notes: The order matters. Deploying dark separates the release risk from the behaviour change, and the flag lets us pilot one hospital rather than the whole cluster.

slides.title: If it goes wrong

cards.title: Turn the flag off
cards.body: Per hospital, no deployment. The merge keeps working and the trigger carries on as before.

cards.title: Revert the service
cards.body: Only needed if the problem is outside blood category handling — the A29 subscription goes with it.

cards.title: Restore the trigger
cards.body: Only if it has already been retired. Until then it is still running and needs nothing.

slides.notes: The first option covers almost every scenario and takes effect immediately, which is the main argument for gating this behind setup rather than shipping it unconditionally.
